questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The founding of NATO and the Warsaw Pact in 1955
The Soviet blockade of West Berlin and the Western airlift response
The Marshall Plan and its economic results across Europe
The Potsdam Agreement's terms for Poland's borders
questions.explain: It covers the 1948-49 blockade and airlift plus the postwar background that led up to them.

questions.q: What did the Soviets offer in exchange for dropping the blockade?
options: That the Western Allies leave Germany altogether by 1949
That the Allies withdraw the Deutsche Mark from West Berlin
That the Allies share control of Berlin's air corridors
That Britain and America end their airlift flights
questions.explain: The Soviets offered to drop it if the Western Allies withdrew the newly introduced Deutsche Mark from West Berlin.

questions.q: At the height of the airlift, how often did a plane reach West Berlin?
options: Every thirty seconds
Every five minutes
Every hour
Every ten seconds
questions.explain: At the height of the airlift, one plane reached West Berlin every thirty seconds.

questions.q: Which zones were combined on 1 January 1947 to form the Bizone?
options: French and Soviet
American and French
American and British
British and Soviet
questions.explain: The British and United States occupation zones were combined into the Bizone.

questions.q: Why did the Americans and British keep flying supplies after the blockade ended?
options: They feared the Soviets might resume the blockade
Berlin still needed materials to rebuild its ruins
The airlift was contractually required to run to September
East Berlin had formally requested more supplies
questions.explain: They worried the Soviets would resume the blockade or were only trying to disrupt Western supply lines.
